# Test fixtures

Raw vendor API responses for the account mappers. Files marked **official** are
the vendors' own published samples, copied verbatim, so the parsers are tested
against the real response shapes rather than shapes we assumed. Files marked
**constructed** are built in those same shapes to cover cases the official
samples don't.

## Xero

| File | Source |
|---|---|
| `xero/trial_balance.official.json` | **Official.** The `GET /Reports/TrialBalance` example from Xero's OpenAPI spec ([XeroAPI/Xero-OpenAPI](https://github.com/XeroAPI/Xero-OpenAPI), `xero_accounting.yaml`), converted from YAML to JSON. |
| `xero/tax_types.json` | **Official.** The `TaxType` enum from the same spec (123 values, most for other countries), used to check the tax type mapping table for typos. |
| `xero/accounts.json` | **Constructed.** A `GET /Accounts` response for the 19 accounts in the official trial balance. AccountID, Name and Code come from the report rows; Type and Class follow the report section; TaxType is illustrative (AU types). |

What the official sample shows:

- Columns are `[Account, Debit, Credit, YTD Debit, YTD Credit]`. Debit/Credit
  are the month's movement; the YTD pair is the as-at balance. A bank account
  shows Debit `0.00` but YTD Debit `7639.04`, and only the YTD columns total to
  the balanced trial balance (`46019.00` both sides).
- Sections have no per-section SummaryRow. The grand total is a final Section
  with `Title: ""` holding only a SummaryRow.
- Account cells read `"Sales (400)"`, name plus code.

## QuickBooks Online

| File | Source |
|---|---|
| `quickbooks/trial_balance.official.json` | **Official.** Intuit's sample `GET /reports/TrialBalance` response. |
| `quickbooks/account_query.official.json` | **Official.** Intuit's sample `select * from Account` response. |
| `quickbooks/taxcode_query.official.json` | **Official.** Intuit's sample `select * from TaxCode` response. |
| `quickbooks/au_company/*.json` | **Constructed.** One consistent AU company (trial balance, accounts, tax codes) in Intuit's shapes. |

The official QuickBooks files come from
`https://static.developer.intuit.com/JSONObjects/CodesModelsJsonObjects_v2.json`,
the data the developer.intuit.com API reference renders. They are from
different sample companies, so ids don't line up across files, and the sample
trial balance is abridged (its rows don't add up to its TOTAL).

What the official samples show:

- The trial balance is flat: account rows with **no `type` field**, then a
  `{ type: "Section", group: "GrandTotal" }` row with only a `Summary`.
- `Header.EndPeriod` is the as-of date.
- TaxCode ids are per company and not always numeric (`"TAX"`, `"NON"`, and
  id `"2"` is "California" in the sample), so tax codes are resolved by name.

The AU company is built to exercise:

- a balanced trial balance whose GrandTotal (`64010.00`) matches its rows
- a negative credit-card balance (`-120.00` in the Credit column)
- an account on the trial balance but not in the Account list (id `99`)
- an account in the Account list but not on the trial balance (id `73`)
- accounts with no `TaxCodeRef`, and an "Input tax" code with no client code
- AU tax code names as Intuit's AU docs list them (`GST`, `GST free`,
  `GST free export`, `GST on capital`, `GST on non-capital`,
  `GST-free non-capital`, `Input tax`, `Out of Scope`)

The AU company JSON is generated by `quickbooks/au_company/generate.js`. Edit
that and rerun it rather than hand-editing the JSON, so the GrandTotal stays
in step with the rows:

```
node test/fixtures/quickbooks/au_company/generate.js test/fixtures/quickbooks/au_company
```
